authors: Petrov, I.; Carroll, J.; Denny, E.
title: Communicating car costs: Results from stated and revealed preference experiments
primary_locator: Publisher-indexed abstract, discussion and conclusion; Transportation Research Part D 147, 104921. DOI redirect failed in read tool; original publisher search text available.
design: Irish online discrete choice experiment and showroom randomized controlled trial
observed_endpoint: Hypothetical drivetrain choice versus actual showroom car choices
finding: Longer-horizon monetary cost information affected hypothetical BEV choice; the showroom trial did not detect an overall effect on drivetrain choice or efficiency/emissions of cars sold.
limits: A null detected effect in this setting is not proof of zero effect everywhere. No verified Auto2000 effect size or portable uplift.
transferability: Mechanism counterevidence, not Indonesian effect estimation.

authors: Bernardic, U.; Cerruti, D.; Filippini, M.; Savelsberg, J.; Ugazio, G.
title: De-biasing electric vehicle adoption with personalized nudging
primary_locator: ETH Zurich working paper 24/390 and author-hosted abstract; UK sample described in official presentation.
design: Randomized information experiment with 3,181 car owners; working paper
observed_endpoint: Stated purchase preference, not confirmed vehicle delivery
finding: Personalized driving/parking-based information, especially TCO, increased BEV purchase preference in the reported experiment.
limits: Working-paper evidence; selection and foreign context; preferences do not establish sales, margins or branch adoption.
transferability: Supports plausibility of personalized fit information while leaving commercial realization unresolved.

authors: Gore, C.; Iogansen, X.; Kneifel, J.; Helveston, J. P.
title: Data Collection Instrument: Consumer Valuation of Battery Health Information in Used Electric Vehicle Markets
primary_locator: NIST DCI 008, abstract PDF p4 and survey instrument; November2025.
design: Proposed survey and discrete choice instrument
observed_endpoint: Study design, not reported estimated price premium
finding: The instrument varies ordinary used-car attributes and battery-specific information to investigate valuation. It does not itself report a measured certificate premium.
limits: Cannot be cited as completed causal evidence that certification raises trade-in offers.
transferability: A useful distinction between a research question and a result.

authors: Webb, D.; Gore, C.; Kneifel, J.
title: Consumer Perspectives on Battery Electric Vehicles: An Analysis of Battery Information and Knowledge
primary_locator: NIST TN2328, abstract PDF p4; validated sample printed p8/PDF16; survey design printed p4; question wording printed p6.
design: 2023 U.S. survey of1,490 individuals, including490 BEV owners
observed_endpoint: Perceived usefulness, concerns and stated next-vehicle likelihood
finding: Respondents found battery lifetime/range information useful; source questions distinguish guarantee, federal rating, manufacturer warranty and industry rating.
limits: Neither actual appraiser acceptance nor a causal transaction-price premium is measured. Source-specific sample differs from other NIST analyses.
transferability: Information types are separable; magnitude is not an Indonesian estimate.

authors: Roberson, L. A.; Helveston, J. P.
title: Not all subsidies are equal: Measuring preferences for electric vehicle financial incentives
primary_locator: Author-hosted original abstract; Environmental Research Letters17,084003.
finding: Immediate rebates were valued more than delayed or differently delivered tax benefits, with subgroup differences.
limits: Tax incentives differ from financing insurance premiums. No dollar value or policy effect is transferred to Auto2000.
transferability: Qualitative support for separating timing and nominal amount.

authors: Roberson, L. A.; Pantha, S.; Helveston, J. P.
title: Battery-powered bargains? Assessing electric vehicle resale value in the United States
primary_locator: Author-hosted original abstract; Environmental Research Letters19,054053.
design: Published observational analysis of roughly9million U.S. online used-car listings2016-2022
observed_endpoint: Listing values and modeled retention, not necessarily completed transaction prices
finding: Retention patterns vary by model year, range and brand, while incentives and market shocks also matter.
limits: The9million rows were used by that study, not acquired by this project. Listed value differs from transaction price; no Indonesian certificate effect.
transferability: Challenges a battery-only explanation of resale value.

authors: Loh, W. S.; Noland, R. B.
title: Concerns expressed by used electric vehicle owners based on surveying social media
primary_locator: Rutgers authors institutional publication record and original publisher abstract.
design: Survey recruited through used-EV Facebook/Reddit communities, Sep-Oct2022;1,669responses,1,167usable
observed_endpoint: Reported concerns among self-selected U.S. used-EV owners
finding: Price, battery performance and public charging are prominent concerns; lower-income concern differs.
limits: This is a recruited survey, not passive social-media scraping or a representative Indonesia sample. Underlying Rutgers data page returned403; raw survey was not acquired.
transferability: Highlights household heterogeneity and survivor/selection limits.
